title: Canadian system of government
examples: What is the main job of the Canadian Parliament?
How does the Charter protect my rights?
What is the difference between federal and provincial law?

explain.say: Today we learn about the Canadian system of government.
The Parliament is where laws for Canada are made.
The House of Commons represents the elected members of the people.
The Charter of Rights and Freedoms protects basic rights for all people.
For example, the Charter guarantees freedom of expression.
In daily life, if a rule seems unfair, you can check it against the Charter.

faq.q: What is the main job of the Canadian Parliament?
faq.a: The Parliament is the group where laws for the entire country are created and debated. It involves elected representatives from different parts of Canada.
asks: Who makes the rules for Canada?

faq.q: Does the Charter protect me from all unfair rules?
faq.a: The Charter protects fundamental rights, but these rights can sometimes be limited by law if it is necessary for public safety. It sets a high standard for rights.
asks: Are my rights absolute in Canada?
What are the limits of the Charter?

faq.q: What is the difference between the Commons and the Senate?
faq.a: The House of Commons has members directly elected by the people. The Senate is a body that reviews and amends the laws passed by the Commons.
asks: Which body represents the people directly?
What role does the Senate play?

faq.q: If my rights are limited, how do I challenge it?
faq.a: You can challenge a law by arguing that it violates your rights under the Charter. This usually involves legal processes in the courts.
asks: Can I sue the government over rights?
What is the legal process for rights violations?

faq.q: Are the rights in the Charter the same everywhere in Canada?
faq.a: The Charter sets national standards, but provinces and territories can have their own laws that must still respect the fundamental rights outlined in the Charter.
asks: Do provinces have their own rights laws?

facts: The Canadian Parliament has two main chambers: the House of Commons and the Senate.
The Charter of Rights and Freedoms guarantees rights like freedom of speech and religion.
Laws passed by the Parliament must respect the fundamental rights listed in the Charter.
The House of Commons members are chosen through elections by the Canadian voters.

quiz.say: Which body is directly elected by the people to represent them in law-making?
quiz.why: The House of Commons is where the majority of elected representatives debate and pass laws for Canada.

wrong.1: The Senate is not directly elected by the general public.
wrong.2: Courts interpret laws; they do not create them.
wrong.3: The Prime Minister leads the government but does not represent the entire elected body.

quiz.say: If a new law limits peaceful assembly, which document could be used to challenge it?
quiz.why: The Charter provides the fundamental legal framework against which rights-limiting laws are measured.

wrong.0: Bylaws are local rules and do not override national constitutional rights.
wrong.1: Tradition is not a legally enforceable right against the state.
wrong.2: While related, the Charter specifically details the individual rights that are protected.

quiz.say: The process of making a law involves debate in the Commons, review by the Senate, and final assent. This shows the system is:
quiz.why: Having multiple bodies review laws prevents any single group from having too much power.

wrong.0: A monarchy is a system ruled by a king or queen, which is not the current system.
wrong.1: Unicameral means having only one chamber, but Canada has two.
wrong.3: Direct democracy means every citizen votes on every law, which is not the system used.
